title: The Horse and the Ass
originalTitle: The Horse and the Ass · English
place: A road and battlefield in ancient Greece
sourceAuthor: Aesop; selected and retold by Joseph Jacobs
note: Joseph Jacobs’s public-domain prose is reproduced directly; only page divisions are editorial. The cover is the matching “Ass and the Charger” plate from Project Gutenberg ebook 18732 (images/image29.png). No other suitable source plates were found, so the turning point and ending are new collection illustrations in a historically appropriate ancient Greek setting.

rights.basis: The 1894 source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A richly harnessed horse and a burdened ass travel along a road.

pageArt.alt: The harnessed horse charges into battle while the ass remains on the road.
The ass stands beside the mortally wounded horse after the battle.

scenes: A Horse and an Ass were travelling together, the Horse prancing along in its fine trappings, the Ass carrying with difficulty the heavy weight in its panniers. “I wish I were you,” sighed the Ass; “nothing to do and well fed, and all that fine harness upon you.”
Next day, however, there was a great battle, and the Horse was wounded to death in the final charge of the day.
His friend, the Ass, happened to pass by shortly afterwards and found him on the point of death. “I was wrong,” said the Ass:
